Definition: Extent to which the national digital identity system is integrated with the data exchange for identity verification and authentication
Comments: Morocco launched a national digital identity platform in May 2022. Citizens can scan their NFC-enabled CNIE (national electronic identity card) to create a digital ID using the My Digital Identity app. The platform is based on DGSN's Trusted Third Party platform, sharing exact personal data from identity cards with service providers. Supports fingerprint, face recognition, or OTP multi-factor authentication. Digital ID is integrated with multiple public and private online services. Score 4: partially integrated.
revision_notes: Original three sources fetched and confirmed as genuine and on-topic (NFCW, Digital Watch Observatory, We Are Tech all describe the May 2022 launch of the DGSN/ADD digital identity platform and September 2022 interoperability platform). Fresher evidence located: DGSN's 2024 annual report (via Barlamantoday and La Verite) shows the Trusted Third Party/Digital Identity platform (CNIE 2.0) had grown to over 30 public and private institutions with direct integration by end-2024, including the Ministry of Justice, tax and customs authorities, and banks, with the Ministry of Health also brought in via a 2024 framework agreement. Biometric Update (Sept 2025) and a May 2025 DGSN-Ministry of Digital Transition framework agreement confirm continued expansion (90+ service providers integrated or integrating, 2.5m active Mon e-ID users, 7m+ transactions since 2022), explicitly accelerated after 2025 cyberattacks. This is extensive but still described as partial/ongoing rollout ('integrated or in the process of integration'), not universal coverage of the data exchange, so the original score of 4 (Partially integrated) is confirmed rather than upgraded to 5. Value code unchanged; evidence and sourcing refreshed to 2025.
revised_comments: Morocco's national digital identity platform, jointly operated by the Direction Générale de la Sûreté Nationale (DGSN) and the Agence de Développement du Digital (ADD) since May 2022, is partially integrated with government service delivery. Citizens use the NFC-enabled CNIE 2.0 card or the 'Mon e-ID' / My Digital Identity mobile app to authenticate via biometrics, PIN/OTP or QR code through the DGSN Trusted Third Party platform. By end-2024 more than 30 public and private institutions had direct integration agreements, including the Ministry of Justice, the Directorate General of Taxes, Customs, the Ministry of Health, national banks and insurers, with over 90 service providers integrated or in the process of integrating as of 2025. Adoption accelerated further in 2025 following a wave of cyberattacks that prompted several agencies (including CNSS and tax authorities) to fast-track digital ID-based authentication, with roughly 2.5 million active users and over 7 million verified transactions recorded since launch. Coverage remains partial rather than universal across the full data exchange ecosystem.

Definition: Integration of health records, patient registration, immunization data, and health insurance into data exchange
Comments: Health was one of the sectors where Plan Maroc Numeric 2013 'did not fully meet expectations' per Oxford Business Group (2016). E-health services are planned under Digital Morocco 2030. The interoperability platform launched 2022 does not specifically mention health as a connected system. Score 2: planned.
revision_notes: Both cited sources were fetched; the 2016 Oxford Business Group report predates the current data exchange entirely and the Digital Morocco 2030 resource only describes general e-government ambitions without confirming health-sector status, so the 'planned' score rested on weak, dated evidence rather than direct confirmation. Fresher, more direct evidence found: in 2024 the Ministry of Health and Social Protection, the National Social Security Fund (CNSS) and the Agence de Développement du Digital (ADD) signed an agreement to unify the Shared Medical Record and Electronic Care Sheet through a common interface (reported in a 2026 MDPI review), and the Ministry of Health was named among DGSN's 2024 CNIE digital-identity framework-agreement partners. Most significantly, the MOHIM (Morocco Health Interoperability and Maturity Lab) programme was launched following GITEX Africa 2025, building a sovereign national interoperability framework (CI-SIS Morocco) with IHE Catalyst, running Projectathons/Connectathons and targeting a Pan-African Connectathon in October 2026. Academic reviews (2025-2026) still describe the underlying health information system as fragmented, with an 'absence of an integrated national architecture', confirming integration is underway but not yet achieved. This moves the score from 'Planned' (2) to 'Under development' (3), reflecting active, resourced implementation rather than a mere stated intention.
revised_comments: Morocco's health system integration into the wider data exchange is under active development rather than merely planned. In 2024 the Ministry of Health and Social Protection, the National Social Security Fund and the Agence de Développement du Digital agreed to unify the Shared Medical Record and Electronic Care Sheet through a common interface, and the Ministry of Health was included among the sectors granted access to the DGSN digital-identity Trusted Third Party platform. Since 2025, the MOHIM (Morocco Health Interoperability and Maturity Lab) programme, led by Mohammed V University's Center for e-Health Innovation with the Ministry of Health and international partner IHE Catalyst, is building a sovereign national health interoperability framework (CI-SIS Morocco) aligned with HL7 FHIR, DICOM and SNOMED CT standards, validated through Projectathons and Connectathons, with a Pan-African Connectathon planned for October 2026. Independent academic reviews confirm that health information systems remain fragmented and not yet governed by an integrated national architecture, indicating that integration is underway but not yet complete.
